title: A Sow's Ear
subtitle: To think the old man believed he'd make a silk purse of it.

items.text: Side Room, School of Mei
Inside the room, a few Yao gather around Mayfly, helping her trim the fresh herbs she picked from the mountains.

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: Now that you know the path, you can go up the hill at your leisure and gather the elixir ingredients yourself. A little walk in the forest will do you good.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Thank you. I know the elixir helps with the practice, but isn't it a little unsettling, harvesting these herbs like this?

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: What's the matter? They're only plants, too young to form any spirit yet. It's not as if you're cutting down one of your own.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Mayfly! Oh, uh, I mean Sister Mayfly, I thought that I should come check on you. See how you're getting on.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Look at that. Someone finally discovered the door. Though not much of a knocker, are you?

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: Good day, Grandmaster.
Paper Heron nods to the Yao, then walks around Mayfly, looking left and right.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: What? What is it? You're giving me the withers.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You've followed Rén's teachings for a few days now, hm? How do you feel?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Heron, you've asked me this a few times already.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I'm well, just as I was yesterday and the day before that. My strength's improving. I feel light and full of energy, even after a long day in the mountains.
Paper Heron puts her hands behind her back and circles Mayfly two more times, nodding each time.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: That's good. That's good then. Are you certain everything's fine? Nothing feels strange at all?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Absolutely!
Mayfly pats her chest as if to prove her health.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Why do you keep asking? Is something troubling you?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Nothing makes me happier than seeing you well. But may I ask have you felt anything out of place while practicing Rén's methods?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Out of place? I don't know. But I've moved on to the second stage, "concentration and visualization."
She sits in a meditation pose and makes a hand gesture to cast an incantation.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Master Rén said that to meditate, I must sit in silence, concentrating my mind on an object and visualizing the inner deities until I find their presence. With consistent practice, the path to longevity will reveal itself.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: That Mei tree nearby really is an ideal object to focus on. It seems to have been there for over a thousand years. Maybe it really does have a connection to the spiritual world.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Are those her words?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Her exact words! I meditate about that tree day and night. I even see it in my dreams sometimes.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: And Master Rén has been most generous. She even helps the other students using the power of her sword. How did she explain it?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Something like using the sword to clear the blockage in their body, freeing the flow of Qi, so they can advance more quickly with their training.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: The first time I saw it, I almost thought she was about to poke a few holes in me. But instead, she just swiped it above my head, just like you did at the parade.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I even asked Brother Yam to teach me something from the third stage. You should see how well I can do it already.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Posture one, "Breeze in the Lungs." Face north, feet spread as wide as the shoulders.
She chants the words and shows Paper Heron what she has learned.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Master Rén told us that we must cultivate our bodies to align with the movement of Qi. Only then can our mortal flesh be prepared for longevity.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: She said the cultivation would take about two months.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Two months? Those were her words?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: That's right.
Hearing Mayfly's words, Paper Heron's face changes. A hint of sternness cuts across her brow.

items.speaker: Butterfly
items.text: *panting*
Butterfly bursts in, panting and waving his hands.

items.speaker: Butterfly
items.text: Wonderful news! Karma finally came for that heartless Chief Constable Chéng!

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Chéng?
Hearing this, the other Yao gather around.

items.speaker: Hedgehog
items.text: You mean that grumpy, self-righteous constable that's been hunting us night and day?

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: I heard that he's been interrogating Yao, plucking his captive's hairs one by one.

items.speaker: Butterfly
items.text: Yes, that's him. What a pig! No offense to pigs!

items.speaker: Butterfly
items.text: I guess brutality must run in his blood. His family used to be bandits until they worked their way into the military. Not that they lasted long as soldiers. His own father turned out to be a crook!

items.speaker: Butterfly
items.text: He cut ties with his father to keep his post. But I don't believe it. If he's willing to throw us all behind bars just to make himself look good, then he's just as bad as the rest of them!

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: I'll bet he's rotten to the core. But what do you mean by "karma came for him"? Ah, tell us what happened.
Butterfly seizes the moment with excitement as he proceeds to describe the fire at the chief constable's home.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Isn't that the man we met at the gate?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I believe so.
Her response is quick and muted, intending not to interrupt the clamor of the Yao.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I just don't understand why he hates us so much. We haven't hurt anyone. We just want to spread the Method of Longevity.

items.speaker: Hedgehog
items.text: Hardly a surprise. Those with long lives seldom care for the short-lived.
The words bring a harsh chill to the air as the other Yao look at each other and then to Paper Heron.

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: Hedgehog! The grandmaster is still here.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Please, speak your mind. It is every creature's right.
Her words do little to break the sudden chill until Butterfly steers things back on topic.

items.speaker: Butterfly
items.text: Oh! I nearly forgot that awful chief had nearly locked up our grandmaster!

items.speaker: Butterfly
items.text: Grandmaster, did you start the fire to avenge us?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Haha. No, I didn't. Though if anyone questions you on the matter, you may give them my name.

items.speaker: Butterfly
items.text: Grandmaster ...
Hearing this, all the Yao look at Paper Heron with awe.

items.speaker: Butterfly
items.text: It is a great honor to study under an avenging hero like you.

items.speaker: Butterfly
items.text: Please accept our humblest gratitude.

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: Thank you. Thank you for your heroic deeds.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Aha ...
Their undeserved praise lands somewhere between funny and vexing, yet she can't help but realize the situation is growing beyond her control.

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: The grandmaster has taken our interests to heart, and we must repay her with our greatest effort. We must achieve longevity and spread the school's name.

items.speaker: All Yao
items.text: Achieve longevity! Spread the school's name!
The room has become a hubbub of cheers and excitement. But Mayfly does not seem to be participating. She stares up blankly, spots dancing in her vision like fireflies at dusk.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Huh, I ... What's going on?

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: Mayfly? Are you alright?
In a moment, Mayfly feels the world spin beneath her feet.
As she tumbles, she sees Paper Heron glide toward her. Then all goes dark.
Yamen, Ancient Zhu County
The next day's sun rises as usual, but the Yamen's constables have a new topic to discuss.

items.speaker: Constable I
items.text: Did you hear? Those gentlemen we met yesterday have all fallen ill.

items.speaker: Constable I
items.text: It seems they've all been taken by a strange fever. Some fainted in an instant, while others went running and yelling on the streets in their undergarments. It was chaos.

items.speaker: Constable I
items.text: The chief was right. Whatever they were doing must have been dangerous.

items.speaker: Constable II
items.text: But I heard they hired a Daoist who cured them with nothing but water and a pinch of talisman ashes.

items.speaker: Constable I
items.text: Hmph. Well, that was easy. Shame the chief wasn't so lucky. To think a man could lose his home simply for doing his duty!

items.speaker: Constable II
items.text: Well, we don't know what caused the fire, do we?

items.speaker: Constable I
items.text: What else could it be? You were there. I think the chief found something important, and now they're desperate to get rid of him.

items.speaker: Constable II
items.text: I'm just glad I was on guard duty.
A shadow passes before the two men. They're struck silent with fear. But Chéng Héguāng does not even seem to notice them as he walks straight into the Yamen hall.
From his high seat, Lì Huìfēng looks at a plaque on the wall.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Héguāng, I understand it was your house that caught fire last night.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: It was.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: It's a great relief to see you unharmed.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: But I'm sorry for your loss. Take a few days. Find another place to stay and get some rest, will you?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Much appreciated, Commander. That is precisely why I came.
Chéng Héguāng bows and then pours out his prepared words. It's clear immediately that he's had little rest.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I was up late reviewing some case files. As it happened, the arsonists startled a cat as they approached. I was able to spy them from my window. Though I couldn't stop them in time.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: They were all Yao. I'm quite certain of it, as retaliation for the arrests I've made.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Commander Lì, if I, a trained officer, couldn't protect my home from their schemes, what hope do the ordinary townspeople have?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Please, permit me to bring them to justice and anyone else who shields them!

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: You—

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I know the Yamen is short-staffed. I won't ask for anyone's help until I have solid evidence.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Now, I must take my leave. Good day, Commander!
He does not wait for Lì Huìfēng to say more and turns to leave.
High above them, the Yamen's bell is stirred by the wind, ringing out a long, clear note.
